newsitem.title: UK: Mideast crude tankers stronger, no weakness seen.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crude tankers stronger, no weakness seen.

text.p: Crude oil charter rates in the world's key lifting area, the Middle East Gulf, edged up to fresh post-Gulf War highs on Tuesday.
Rates in other sectors were also stronger.
The dominant Middle East chartering sector saw rates for trips to Japan edge up to W95 on VLCCs with a trip to South Korea done at W92.5. Westwards 250,000 tonners were talked around W75.
Shipbrokers said there was a shortage of good quality ships set against strong demand from Asian refiners.
"The worm has turned; owners are asking for high numbers and getting them," said one broker.

The Mediterranean market continues to ride on the back of increased business thanks to Iraqi exports out of Ceyhan. Shipping sources said 80,000 tonners were attacting up to W110 on cross Med trips with a high of W112.5 thought done today.
Suezmaxes (130,000 tonners) were also capitalising on the increased demand from charterers and vessels were able to secure around W92-95.
The buoyant Med market has helped underpin an already tight North Sea sector, shippers said.
80,000 tonners on inter UKC work have gained five points to W140 with further rate gains envisaged.
"There are still a few cargoes uncovered so its looking good for the (ship)owners," said one broker.
Freight rates in West Africa were also stronger with 130,000 tonners heading to the U.S. able to attract W100, up a few points.
The Caribbean up U.S. coast market was steady, with 70,000 tonners attracting W145.
